messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am trying to obtain detection histories for multiple species, using the code below:

for (i in 1:length(animal)){
  occ_data[[i]] <- detectionHistory(recordTable = recordTab,
                                    camOp = cam_op,
                                    species = animal[i],
                                    output = output,
                                    stationCol = "Station",
                                    speciesCol = "Species",
                                    recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                    recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                                    occasionLength = 1,
                                    day1 = "survey",
                                    includeEffort = F,
                                    datesAsOccasionNames = T,
                                    timeZone = "Asia/Singapore"
                                    )
}

However, this error message pops up: "Error: Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated. This is a bug. I'm Sorry. Please report it.". May I know what this means, and how I can possibly avoid this? Please do let me know if more information is required.

Thank you so much.

Best regards,
Joejyn

messages.subject: Re: Merging studies from different years
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
and sorry for the late reply. Can you please share the code you used that led to the error? Right now I don't even know which function caused it.
You can specify a season / session in the camera trap table and then pass that to cameraOperation() with the argument sessionCol. That was intended for such situations, combining data from multiple season (at the same locations).
Please see vignette 3 for details:
https://jniedballa.github.io/camtrapR/articles/camtrapr3.html#multi-season-occupancy-analyses

If the studies were carried out at different locations (they don't have the same camera trap stations) then you can simply rbind() the camera trap tables and the record tables and then continue with cameraOperation / detectionMatrix. In that case you can e.g. include a "year" covariate in the models to account for the differences between the studies.

Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error: Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated
messages.subject_clean: Error: Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joejyn,
this is an unexprected situation and a bug. Internally, the function calculates an occasion number for a record that is higher than the number of columns in the detection matrix. Therefore the occasion cannot be assigned and I put an error there in case that should ever happen unexpectedly (this is the first time I believe).
It may have to do with occasionLength = 1 and I wouldn't be surprised if it works with higher numbers. Can you check that please? But nevertheless, it is still a bug.
Please feel free to share a small reproducible example so I can fix the issue (R workspace and code). Feel free to share it privately to my email as a Dropbox / GDrive link if you don't want it to be public.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error: Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated
messages.subject_clean: Error: Occasions exceeding total number of occasions calculated
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jürgen,

Thanks for the reply. After looking at how the error message was produced by looking at the source code, I managed to find the problem. There was a higher number of occasions for my data because I had missing data in the middle of my survey period (e.g. survey period was from 1 Oct to 30 Nov, but no data was available for 22 Oct to 30 Oct). And since the number of occasions was calculated by using the first and last date, the detection matrix had less columns than the calculated number of occasions.

Do let me know if you require more information on how to reproduce the bug.

Thanks and best regards,
Joejyn

Hi,
I haven't seen this problem before so I'm afraid I don't know how to fix it. When I google the error code 65535 the results indicate it is a file system error (e.g. here <https://answers.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/forum/all/file-system-error-65535-when-trying-to-run-exe/b2989585-e75b-e011-8dfc-68b599b31bf5>).
Do you get the problem only with exiftool or with other software too?

Can you try running one of the exiftool calls directly in the command prompt (cmd.exe), e.g.:

exiftool -q -f -t -r -Directory -FileName -EXIF:DateTimeOriginal -ext JPG "c:/Users/Audrey/Desktop/Research Proposal/camtrapR/Station Folders/Carriage Hill CAT"

That way we can make sure it has nothing to do with R. If the problem persists, try reinstalling exiftool.
If that fails, try running the Windows system file checker tool to make sure the hard disk is ok.

Alternatively, to make sure the code is ok, you could try running the same code on a different machine.
I'm sorry I can't be more specific. It doesn't seem to be a camtrapR issue from what I can see.
Let me know how it goes.
Best,
Jürgen
